title: Tharoor Calls for Predictable China Ties Not Weaponised Against India
excerpt: At the NDTV World Summit, Shashi Tharoor cited China's border behaviour and its support for Pakistan during Operation Sindoor as the political reaction to the ITBP chief's remarks widened.
body:
• Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said on Friday that India needs predictable ties with China that are not weaponised against it, speaking at the NDTV World Summit amid the row over the ITBP chief's remarks.
  • Tharoor said India has many frustrations with China for good reason, citing behaviour on the borders, territory being nibbled away, and China's overt support for Pakistan during Operation Sindoor.
  • The reaction follows ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Kapur's statement that face-offs with Chinese troops happened at several locations in Arunachal Pradesh in recent days and continue — a story The Videshi covered earlier today.
  • Government sources have since said Kapur's comments reflected routine preparedness and were not linked to any specific incident, and an official ITBP statement may follow — the next development to watch.

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday called for a predictable relationship with China that cannot be turned against India, as the political reaction widened to remarks by the chief of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police about continuing face-offs along the Arunachal Pradesh frontier. Speaking at the NDTV World Summit, Tharoor said India has "very many frustrations with China for good reason," according to NDTV.

"The way in which China has behaved on our borders, the way in which they've nibbled away at our territory, their overt support for Pakistan during the brief conflict (Op Sindoor) between our two countries last year is worrying."

— Shashi Tharoor, Congress MP, at the NDTV World Summit

Tharoor's formulation — captured in NDTV's headline as the need for "predictable ties which are not weaponised against us" — frames the opposition's position in this row: not a call to cut engagement with Beijing, but a demand that the terms of engagement stop shifting against India on the border, on territory and through China's backing of Pakistan.

The remarks that set off the row

The reaction follows comments on Thursday by ITBP Director General Shatrujeet Kapur, who told personnel at a force base in Alwar, Rajasthan, that face-offs with Chinese troops had occurred at several locations in Arunachal Pradesh in recent days and that the situation was continuing. Kapur also highlighted a new combat unit, the Shaurya Commandos, saying its personnel had demonstrated their capabilities during the ongoing face-offs. The Videshi reported those remarks earlier today: Face-Offs With China Happened in Arunachal in Past Few Days and Continue, ITBP Chief Says.

https://x.com/ndtv/status/2113573647080460436

Other Congress voices reacted more sharply. Rajya Sabha MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X that India has been paying the price for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's "clean chit" to China on June 19, 2020, and said that while the government's "calibrated concessions to China continue," the ITBP chief had lauded the force's performance in recent face-offs with the People's Liberation Army, on which there had been "a deafening silence" from the prime minister and his establishment, according to the Daily Jagran.

The government's response

Government sources moved to narrow the meaning of Kapur's comments. Sources told IANS the remarks were made in the context of routine operational preparedness and force deployment along the frontier and were not linked to any specific incident. The ITBP, they said, operates in accordance with government policies, instructions and standard operating procedures, and the force may issue an official statement soon.

That reading sits alongside recent official assessments. Last month, Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani said at the NDTV Defence Summit that the situation along the border was stable and there was no cause for concern, IANS reported. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar stressed last week that maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas was essential for normalising relations, and cautioned that any disruption along the frontier would have consequences for bilateral ties.

Why predictability is the contested word

India and China have been working to rebuild relations after reaching an understanding in October 2024 to resolve the military standoff in eastern Ladakh, which lasted more than four years. Chinese President Xi Jinping visited India on September 12-13 for the BRICS Summit, his first visit in seven years, and held bilateral talks with Modi. The ITBP, established in 1962, guards the 3,488-kilometre Line of Actual Control, and Kapur — who is scheduled to retire at the end of this month — used the same Alwar address to argue for modernisation, including drones and new commando units in every border battalion.

Tharoor's intervention separates two arguments the row has blurred: whether a specific new incident occurred in Arunachal Pradesh, which government sources deny, and whether the post-2024 thaw has produced the predictable, non-coercive relationship India says it needs. The practical test is the official ITBP statement sources say may come.
